topics.title: Vol II: Special Responses — Airports, Freeway, Power & Solar (205.13–205.24) (Part 1)
topics.sub: Aircraft alerts and staging at Sky Harbor, Goodyear, Deer Valley and Glendale; foam units; freeway and Papago Tunnel response; District Van; mutual aid.
concepts: 205.13: Alert 1 = minor trouble, Alert 2 = major trouble (smoke, gear, hydraulics), Alert 3 = actual crash or gear-up landing over 12,500 lbs. The Station 19 captain sets the alert level.
205.13: Cut a foam path from the exit to safety. A fuselage can burn through in 60 seconds. Most deaths come from smoke inhalation. No overhaul until investigators are done.
205.13A/B/C: Alert 1 = one engine. Stage at the Goodyear tower base, inside Deer Valley gate #2, or at the Glendale tower gate #9. Stay off runways until they're closed.
205.14: Foam 34/54 respond automatically to flammable liquid calls. Sky Harbor ARFF goes off airport within 5 miles. Dry chem works best on pressurized or flowing fuel fires.
205.15: Respond Code 2 on the mainline. Go against traffic only at DPS request with traffic stopped. Later units stage Level I near an on-ramp. Form Unified Command with DPS/ADOT.
205.15A: Hydrants every 300 ft, alternating sides. Humats won't fit. Say your unit ID twice on the radio. Stage Level II on Culver St west of Central. Second-due may use the Bus Transit Tunnel.
205.16: The District Van is staffed by cadets or volunteers, requested by on-scene FD only, and responds Code 2. It's not a substitute for an ambulance.
205.17: Mutual aid needs a formal request and the AHJ stays responsible. Minimum 3&1 for structure fires. No hot zone work without a direct dispatch tactical radio link. Over 12 hrs = Statewide plan.

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.13, a pilot reports smoke visible on board and requests emergency equipment at Sky Harbor. What alert category is this?
cards.a: An Alert 2 (major difficulties, positive indication of fire).
cards.why: M.P. 205.13: Alert 2 indicates major difficulties such as a "positive indication of fire (smoke visible) on board the aircraft," faulty landing gear or no hydraulic pressure.
opts: Alert 2
Alert 1
Alert 3
ARFF1A

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.13, a pilot of an aircraft over 12,500 lbs says the landing gear will not extend and they must land gear-up at Sky Harbor. What alert is it?
cards.a: An Alert 3.
cards.why: M.P. 205.13: Alert 3 covers an actual accident and also a pilot of an aircraft over 12,500 pounds indicating the gear will not extend and the aircraft will land gear-up.
opts: Alert 3
Alert 2
Alert 1
ARFF2-1

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.13, who decides the alert category and ARFF response for an aircraft emergency at Sky Harbor?
cards.a: A fire captain at Sky Harbor Airport Fire Station 19.
cards.why: M.P. 205.13: The response "will be dictated by a fire captain at Sky Harbor Airport Fire Station #19," who takes a pessimistic view and selects the most appropriate alert level.
opts: The fire captain at Sky Harbor Fire Station 19
The FAA Control Tower supervisor on duty
The on-duty Phoenix shift commander
The first-arriving battalion chief

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.13, how far from the runway must each ARFF standby position at Sky Harbor be?
cards.a: At least 500 feet away from the runway.
cards.why: M.P. 205.13: Foam 1 stages near the west end, Foam 2 near the east end, Foam 3 near the midpoint, and "each position will be at least 500 feet away from the runway."
opts: At least 500 feet
At least 300 feet
At least 1,000 feet
At least 250 feet

cards.q: You're first in at an aircraft crash where passengers are evacuating through burning fuel. Per M.P. 205.13, how do you create their path of egress?
cards.a: Discharge Class B foam to create a path through the burning liquid from the exit door to a safe area.
cards.why: M.P. 205.13: Assist evacuation "by discharging Class B foam only" to create a path from the escape door to a safe area; if foam is unavailable, use large volumes of water.
opts: Discharge Class B foam to cut a path from the exit door to a safe area
Use straight streams of water to push the fire away from the fuselage
Apply dry chemical only, holding foam back for the fuselage
Wait for all foam units to arrive before applying any agent

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.13, how quickly can fire burn through an aircraft fuselage with direct flame impingement?
cards.a: Within 60 seconds.
cards.why: M.P. 205.13: Protect the fuselage from direct flame impingement "since fire can burn through fuselage within 60 seconds."
opts: Within 60 seconds
Within 3 minutes
Within 5 minutes
Within 30 seconds

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.13 tactical benchmarks, what is the usual cause of fatalities in survivable aircraft crashes?
cards.a: Smoke inhalation, so interior ventilation is started as soon as possible.
cards.why: M.P. 205.13: "Fatalities in survivable aircraft crashes are usually due to smoke inhalation," so provide interior ventilation as soon as possible.
opts: Smoke inhalation
Impact trauma
Burns from fuel fires
Exploding oxygen cylinders

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.13, when can overhaul begin at an aircraft accident?
cards.a: Not until all investigative agencies are finished, unless needed to suppress fire.
cards.why: M.P. 205.13: "Do not allow any overhaul operations to take place until all investigative agencies are finished or unless needed to suppress fire."
opts: Once investigative agencies are finished, unless needed to suppress fire
As soon as the fire is knocked down and all clears are given
After the airline representative approves it at the Command Post
Once the foam blanket has been maintained for 30 minutes

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.13, who is asked to notify the NTSB after an aircraft accident?
cards.a: Command requests the Alarm Room notify the NTSB.
cards.why: M.P. 205.13: "Request the Alarm Room notify the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB)," via the FAA tower or Sky Harbor Communications.
opts: The Alarm Room, at Command's request
The first-arriving company officer
The airline representative at the Command Post
The Police Department liaison

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.13A, what does an Alert 1 response to Goodyear Airport consist of?
cards.a: One engine company.
cards.why: M.P. 205.13A: "An Alert 1 response consists of one (1) Engine Company."
opts: One engine company
Two engine companies and Foam 34
One engine company and one chief
One engine company and one ladder company

cards.q: You're dispatched to an Alert 2 at Goodyear Airport. Per M.P. 205.13A, where do you stage?
cards.a: At the base of the Goodyear Control Tower until the aircraft has landed.
cards.why: M.P. 205.13A: On Alert 1s and 2s, "all fire department units shall respond to the base of the Goodyear Control Tower and stage until the aircraft has landed."
opts: At the base of the Goodyear Control Tower until the aircraft lands
At the airport main entrance gate
At the end of the active runway
At Gate #9 next to the fuel farm

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.13A, which outside agency also responds to an Goodyear Airport Alert 2, and with what?
cards.a: The Goodyear Fire Department, with one engine company and one chief.
cards.why: M.P. 205.13A: On an Alert 2, "the Goodyear Fire Department will respond with one (1) engine company and one (1) chief."
opts: Goodyear Fire, with one engine company and one chief
Avondale Fire, with one engine and one ladder
Luke AFB Fire, with one crash truck
Goodyear Fire, with Foam 34 and a utility truck

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.13B, where do companies stage on an Alert 1 or 2 at Deer Valley Airport?
cards.a: At the main entrance (7th Ave and Deer Valley Rd), just inside gate #2.
cards.why: M.P. 205.13B: Companies respond to the main entrance at 7th Ave. and Deer Valley Rd. and stage "just inside gate #2."
opts: Just inside gate #2 at the main entrance, 7th Ave and Deer Valley Rd
At the base of the Deer Valley Control Tower
At gate #9, which has a Knox box lock
Midfield, at least 500 feet off the runway

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.13B, a Deer Valley Airport Alert 3 response includes two engines, a ladder, a rescue, a utility truck, a BC, and what else if available?
cards.a: T36, if available.
cards.why: M.P. 205.13B: Alert 2 and Alert 3 responses at Deer Valley include "T36 if available."
opts: Foam 34
Foam 54
A brush truck

cards.q: At any of the smaller airports (e.g., Deer Valley), when may you drive on a runway per M.P. 205.13B?
cards.a: Only after a determination that the runway has been closed to all aircraft.
cards.why: M.P. 205.13B: "If traveling on a runway is necessary, do so only after a determination has been made that the runway has been closed to all aircraft."
opts: Only after it's determined the runway is closed to all aircraft
Once the aircraft has come to a complete stop
Any time with lights and siren operating
Only when escorted by an airport operations vehicle

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.13C, where do companies stage on an Alert 1 or 2 at Glendale Airport?
cards.a: At the Glendale Control Tower at gate #9.
cards.why: M.P. 205.13C: All companies "respond to the Glendale Control Tower at gate #9 and stage until the aircraft has landed."
opts: At the Glendale Control Tower at gate #9
Just inside gate #2 at the main entrance
At the base of the runway threshold
At the nearest Glendale fire station

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.13C, where do companies go on a Glendale Airport Alert 3?
cards.a: Directly to the crash site.
cards.why: M.P. 205.13C: "For Alert 3 incidents, all companies shall respond directly to the crash site."
opts: Directly to the crash site
To gate #9 to stage until directed
To the base of the control tower
To a Level II staging area off airport

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.13C, what should responding companies request through dispatch on a Glendale Airport aircraft emergency?
cards.a: The number of passengers on board, the amount of fuel on board, and the aircraft type.
cards.why: M.P. 205.13C: Companies should request "the number of passengers on board, the amount of fuel on board the aircraft, and aircraft type if possible."
opts: Passengers on board, fuel on board, and aircraft type
Pilot's name, flight number, and origin airport
Runway in use, wind speed, and visibility
Cargo manifest, airline contact, and tail number

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.14, which units respond automatically to flammable liquid incidents anywhere in the city?
cards.a: Foam 34 and Foam 54.
cards.why: M.P. 205.14: "Foam 34 and/or 54 will be dispatched automatically to all flammable liquid incidents"; they are automatic response anywhere in the City.
opts: Foam 34 and Foam 54
Attack 19 and Foam 1
Foam 1, Foam 2 and Foam 3
Support 4 and Foam 34

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.14, Sky Harbor ARFF equipment is dispatched off the airport for an aircraft incident within what radius?
cards.a: Within a 5 mile radius.
cards.why: M.P. 205.14: "Sky Harbor ARFF equipment will be dispatched off the airport within a 5 mile radius for an aircraft incident."
opts: 5 miles
3 miles
10 miles
2 miles

cards.q: A tanker is leaking burning fuel under pressure. Per M.P. 205.14, which agent works best on it?
cards.a: Dry chemical agent.
cards.why: M.P. 205.14: "AFFF will not work well on free-flowing burning fuels or fuel burning under pressure. However, dry chemical agent is very effective."
opts: Dry chemical
AFFF foam
Plain water fog
Polar solvent AFFF

cards.q: Command wants Sky Harbor ARFF units for a non-aircraft incident. Per M.P. 205.14, what is required?
cards.a: Coordination with Sky 1 (or designee) to assure FAA Index D is maintained.
cards.why: M.P. 205.14: ARFF requested for any other incident "will require coordination with Sky 1 (or her/his designee) to assure that FAA Index D is maintained."
opts: Coordination with Sky 1 so FAA Index D is kept with the remaining foam units
Approval from the Phoenix shift commander and the FAA tower
Nothing extra; ARFF units respond on any special call
A request through the Airport Duty Manager's office

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.14, how is Foam 34 staffed when it responds?
cards.a: As a 2-piece company with an assigned engine company (normally Engine 34).
cards.why: M.P. 205.14: "Foam 34 will respond as a 2-piece company with an assigned engine company," which assumes the identity of Foam 34; Dispatch assigns another engine if E34 isn't available.
opts: As a 2-piece company with an assigned engine company
By its own dedicated 2-person ARFF crew
By a crew from Station 19 with BC19
By the first-due ladder company's crew

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.15, how do units respond while on the freeway mainline?
cards.a: Code 2, although alternating headlights and rear flashers may be used.
cards.why: M.P. 205.15: "Units responding to calls on the Freeway will respond Code 2 while on the Freeway mainline. However, alternating headlights and rear flashers may be used."
opts: Code 2, though alternating headlights and rear flashers may be used
Code 3 with full lights and siren the whole way
Code 3 until within one mile, then Code 2
Code 2 with no warning lights of any kind

cards.q: DPS advises your best access is to drive against normal freeway traffic. Per M.P. 205.15, when may you do this?
cards.a: Only at the specific request of DPS when it is assured all traffic has been stopped, and you confirm it.
cards.why: M.P. 205.15: Proceed against normal flow "only at the specific request of D.P.S. when it is assured that all traffic has been stopped." Fire units should confirm traffic is stopped.
opts: Only at DPS's specific request, after confirming all traffic is stopped
Any time the officer judges it faster than the frontage road
Only when Command approves it over the radio
Only with a ladder company blocking for you

cards.q: On a multi-unit freeway response, the first unit reports within a mile of the scene. Per M.P. 205.15, what do other units do?
cards.a: Stage Level I, preferably near an on-ramp, to avoid premature commitment.
cards.why: M.P. 205.15: Other approaching units "will then stage Level I, preferably near an on-ramp to avoid premature commitment to the mainline or access frontage."
opts: Stage Level I, preferably near an on-ramp
Proceed directly onto the mainline to the scene
Stage Level II at the nearest fire station
Take the opposite direction and wait at the median

cards.q: You're cancelled en route to a freeway crash by DPS. Per M.P. 205.15, what do you do?
cards.a: Do not proceed into the scene unless re-dispatched.
cards.why: M.P. 205.15: Units canceled en route "should not proceed into the scene unless re-dispatched," since it creates unnecessary congestion.
opts: Don't proceed into the scene unless re-dispatched
Continue in Code 2 to confirm no patients
Proceed to the scene but stay on the shoulder
Stage on the nearest on-ramp for 10 minutes

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.15, who is usually left to watch traffic and set warning devices until DPS arrives?
cards.a: One crew member, usually the Engineer.
cards.why: M.P. 205.15: "Leave one crew member (usually the Engineer) to watch the traffic and set up warning devices until the D.P.S. arrives."

The company officer
The two firefighters together
The first-arriving DPS cadet

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.15, which agencies are key in a freeway Unified Command post?
cards.a: Fire, DPS, ADOT, and city police if freeway traffic is diverted onto city streets.
cards.why: M.P. 205.15: Key agencies are the fire department, DPS, ADOT, "and if freeway traffic is being diverted to city streets, the appropriate city police."

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.15's glossary, how are freeway traffic lanes numbered?
cards.a: Lane No. 1 is nearest the median or center, excluding the H.O.V. lane.

No. 1 is the HOV lane, then count right
No. 1 is the lane nearest the access road

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.15, which freeway term refers to the Papago (I-10)/Black Canyon (I-17) interchange between 19th and 27th Avenues?

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.15A, how often are hydrant cabinets located in the Papago vehicle tunnels?
cards.a: Approximately every 300 feet on alternating sides (600 feet apart on the same side).
cards.why: M.P. 205.15A: Hydrant cabinets are "approximately every 300 feet on alternating sides of the tunnel (600 feet separation on the same side)." Emergency phone cabinets are every 150 feet.
opts: About every 300 feet on alternating sides (600 ft same side)

About every 500 feet on the north wall only

cards.a: Humat valves will not fit into the hydrant boxes; a direct hose connection is required.
cards.why: M.P. 205.15A: "HUMAT VALVES WILL NOT FIT INTO THE HYDRANT BOXES IN THE VEHICLE TUNNELS. A DIRECT HOSE CONNECTION WILL BE REQUIRED."
opts: Humat valves won't fit; a direct hose connection is required
The cabinets are dry and must be charged first
Humats are only allowed on the 2 1/2" fitting

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.15A, how should you start a radio transmission inside the Papago Tunnel?
cards.a: Repeat your company identity twice at the front of the message.
cards.why: M.P. 205.15A: The repeater needs about a half-second to capture, so "companies should repeat their company identity twice" (e.g., "Engine Four, Engine Four to Alarm").

Wait three seconds after keying the mic
Switch to channel 8 before every message
Say "emergency traffic" first

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.15A, where do other companies Level II stage for a significant Papago Tunnel incident?
cards.a: On Culver Street, just west of Central (at the standpipe connection).
cards.why: M.P. 205.15A: "Other companies should Level II Stage on Culver Street, just west of Central," where the tunnel's hydrant standpipe connection is located.

cards.q: Traffic is jammed for a 2-1 in the Papago Tunnel. Per M.P. 205.15A, what should the second-due company consider?

opts: Seal it, secure all power, and let it burn out

Move everyone to channel 1 dispatch

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.17, what is mutual aid?
cards.a: Assistance from one jurisdiction to another, on formal request, when no formal Automatic Aid agreement exists.

opts: Help given on formal request where no automatic aid agreement exists

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.17, who remains ultimately responsible for an incident when mutual aid is provided?
cards.a: The Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ).
cards.why: M.P. 205.17: "The Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) remains ultimately responsible for the incident and must provide incident support."

cards.why: M.P. 205.17: "A 3&1 assignment will be the minimum deployment for a Structure fire or any fire with a report of people trapped."

cards.q: A county island calls in a reported child choking. Per M.P. 205.17, how is it handled?
cards.a: Dispatched without approval, with the closest most appropriate unit(s), as an imminent threat to life.

cards.a: It is deferred to the shift commander of the requested agency for approval.
cards.why: M.P. 205.17: Requests not involving imminent threat to life "(defensive structure or vegetation fire for example) will be deferred to the shift commander of the requested agency."

cards.q: Your mutual aid crew has no direct tactical radio link to Phoenix or Mesa Dispatch. Per M.P. 205.17, what can you do?
cards.a: Do not work in the hot zone; support AHJ resources from outside the hazard zone.

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.17, requests for mutual aid lasting longer than how long fall under the Arizona Statewide Mutual Aid Plan?
cards.a: More than 12 hours.

24 hours
8 hours

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.17, who completes overhaul at a mutual aid incident?
cards.a: The requesting jurisdiction.
cards.why: M.P. 205.17: Assisting resources are released as soon as conditions warrant; "All overhaul operations will be completed by the requesting jurisdiction."

Whichever unit has the most personnel

topics.title: Vol II: Special Responses — Airports, Freeway, Power & Solar (205.13–205.24) (Part 2)
topics.sub: Assisting other agencies, Water Department hazmat notices, power lines, battery storage, solar PV, surgical team response, MR/LA units and drones.
concepts: 205.18: Agencies request Special Ops through the Dispatch Supervisor. Don't enter a warrant site until police declare it safe. Canine teams never search for violent or criminal subjects.
205.19: A Fire Prevention Specialist calls the Water Department about clean-ups using hydrants or hose bibs, so backflow devices are installed.
205.20: Treat every downed line as energized. Tingling feet means step potential, so back away. Occupants stay in the car. No attack on a pole fire until the utility confirms it's de-energized.
205.20A: For a BESS: utility plus a 3&1+ hazmat response, isolate 150 ft (residential: 40 ft), don't open it, fight defensively and let it burn out. Stranded energy remains after disconnects.
205.20B: PV runs up to 600/1000/1500 V DC (residential/commercial/utility). Fog at 10°+ from 20 ft+ after disconnects. Announce PV on the tactical channel. No roof ops on BIPV.
205.22: SERT is ready within 30 minutes. The closest BC picks up the team (2 seats max). A second Command Officer is added. The charting paramedic documents.
205.23: MR = 4-person crew that can't replace an engine. LA = 2-person crew that supports 4-person companies and supplements, not replaces, units on imminent-threat calls.
205.24: The drone PIC's authority is absolute. Max 400 ft AGL. Ground the drone when manned aircraft arrive. VO required at night. No flying within 8 hrs of alcohol. Max 10 consecutive hrs as PIC.

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.18, how does an outside agency request Special Operations/TRT help at a search warrant site?
cards.a: By contacting the Dispatch Supervisor.
cards.why: M.P. 205.18: Any agency requesting on-duty Special Operations personnel or TRT units "shall contact the Dispatch Supervisor." A pre-incident meeting with the Special Operations Duty Officer follows.
opts: Contact the Dispatch Supervisor
Call the nearest fire station captain
Email the Special Operations Chief
Call 911 and request Assist Agency

cards.q: At a search warrant site, when may PFD personnel enter per M.P. 205.18?
cards.a: Only after the appropriate law enforcement agency has deemed the site secured and "safe."
cards.why: M.P. 205.18: "Phoenix Fire Department personnel shall not make entry into the search warrant site until the appropriate law enforcement agency has deemed the site secured and 'safe'."
opts: After law enforcement deems the site secured and safe
As soon as the hazmat team is on scene
Once the Fire Prevention Specialist arrives
After the suspects have left the property

cards.q: A firefighter shows non-critical exposure symptoms after a search warrant. Per M.P. 205.18, where are they transported?
cards.a: Banner Good Samaritan (unless it is a critical life-threatening emergency).
cards.why: M.P. 205.18: Exposed personnel are transported to Banner Good Samaritan if not critical; "critical life threatening injuries require transport to the closest appropriate hospital."
opts: Banner Good Samaritan
The closest hospital, always
The city occupational health clinic
Any trauma center the crew chooses

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.18, PFD canine search teams may NOT be used for which search?
cards.a: Searches involving criminal or violent subjects.
cards.why: M.P. 205.18: "At no time will any Phoenix Fire Department canine search specialist teams and support personnel be used to conduct search operations involving criminal or violent subjects."
opts: Searches for criminal or violent subjects
Lost non-violent adults in a rural area
Missing children in an urban setting
Live victims at a disaster site

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.19, why does the Water Department want notice of hazmat clean-ups?
cards.a: So backflow devices can be installed on hydrants or hose bibs to prevent water main contamination.
cards.why: M.P. 205.19: The Water Department asked to be notified "to ensure that, when required, backflow devices are installed... to prevent water main contamination."
opts: To install backflow devices so water mains aren't contaminated
To shut down all hydrants within one mile
To bill the business for water used
To send a crew to perform decontamination

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.19, who calls the Water Department when a hazmat clean-up may use a hydrant or hose bib?
cards.a: A Fire Prevention Specialist.
cards.why: M.P. 205.19: When clean-up may involve a hydrant or hose bib, "a Fire Prevention Specialist shall call the Water Department's 24-hour number."
opts: A Fire Prevention Specialist
The Incident Commander
The hazmat team captain
The business responsible party

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.19, which activity does the Water Department notification NOT apply to?
cards.a: Fire Department emergency mitigation, overhaul, and FD-conducted decontamination.
cards.why: M.P. 205.19: The procedure "shall not apply to Fire Department activities conducted to mitigate an emergency, overhaul operations, or decontamination activities conducted by Fire Department personnel."
opts: Decon done by Fire Department personnel during the emergency
Clean-up by a hazardous waste contractor
Rinsing of containers after an incident
Decon by the business's own employees

cards.q: You arrive to a downed power line in a yard. Per M.P. 205.20, how do you treat it?
cards.a: Consider it energized with potentially lethal current.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20: "Downed lines must always be considered energized with potentially lethal current."
opts: As energized with potentially lethal current
As dead if no sparking is seen
As de-energized if the lights are out nearby
As safe once the utility is called

cards.q: Approaching a downed line, you feel tingling in your feet. Per M.P. 205.20, what is happening?
cards.a: Step potential from gradient voltage; it's a warning to back away.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20: A voltage difference between your feet is "step potential." A tingling sensation in the feet is a warning to back away. It is worse on wet ground.
opts: Step potential; back away from the area
Touch potential; keep moving to the line
Induction from overhead lines; it's harmless
Reel memory; the line is about to curl

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.20, what classification means a line has been confirmed safe by the utility after grounding?
cards.a: "Dead" — confirmed by utility representatives after grounding the line(s).
cards.why: M.P. 205.20: Equipment is energized, de-energized ("cannot be 100% guaranteed"), or dead (confirmed by utility representatives after grounding).
opts: Dead
De-energized
Isolated
Locked out

cards.q: A power line is down across a car with occupants and no fire. Per M.P. 205.20, what do you tell them?
cards.a: Have the occupants remain inside the vehicle.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20: Do not touch the vehicle and "have occupants remain inside the vehicle" while the utility is requested.
opts: Stay inside the vehicle
Get out and walk away quickly
Step out carefully onto dry ground
Climb out the window and run

cards.q: Fire forces occupants out of a car with a line down on it. Per M.P. 205.20, how should they exit?
cards.a: Open the door, jump free without touching the vehicle and ground at once, and walk away in very small steps.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20: They "should jump free of the vehicle without touching vehicle and ground at the same time; they should walk away from the vehicle with very small steps."
opts: Jump clear without touching car and ground, then shuffle in small steps
Step out holding the door frame, then run
Have firefighters pull them out with a dry rope
Slide out slowly, keeping one hand on the car

cards.q: A power pole is on fire. Per M.P. 205.20, when can you begin a fire attack?
cards.a: Only after the utility representative verifies the equipment is de-energized.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20: "Do not make any fire attack until the utility representative has verified that the electrical equipment has been de-energized."
opts: After the utility rep verifies it's de-energized
Right away, using a fog at the base of the pole
Once the pole has burned through and fallen
After breaker trips are confirmed by Dispatch

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.20, if you must apply water near energized equipment, how should it be done?
cards.a: Use a fog spray at the base of the pole, in short bursts; never spray into the lines.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20: "Never spray directly into the power lines. Use a fog spray at the base of the pole." Short bursts are preferred to avoid being grounded.
opts: Fog spray at the base of the pole in short bursts
A straight stream directly at the lines
A solid stream from at least 20 feet
Continuous fog aimed at the transformer

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.20, during periods of high activity, what may the company officer do at a lines-down call?
cards.a: Leave one crewmember on scene with a radio to wait for the utility company.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20: In periods of high activity, "company officer may choose to leave one (1) crewmember on-scene with a radio to wait for utility company."
opts: Leave one crew member with a radio to wait for the utility
Leave the scene once the area is taped off
Ask a neighbor to watch the line until the utility arrives
Request police to stand by and clear the company

cards.q: You arrive at a commercial BESS that is smoking. Per M.P. 205.20A, what is the recommended initial evacuation distance?
cards.a: 150 feet.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20A: "Isolate the area. Recommended initial evacuation distance is 150 feet. Do not enter the fenced area," except for a savable life/known rescue.
opts: 150 feet
40 feet
300 feet
75 feet

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.20A, why must you NOT open a BESS building or compartment door?
cards.a: Introducing fresh air may result in a deflagration.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20A: "Do not make entry or approach BESS building or compartment. Introducing fresh air may result in a deflagration."
opts: Introducing fresh air may cause a deflagration
It may trip the fire suppression system
The doors are energized with DC current
It voids the vendor's warranty

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.20A, what response should be requested for a BESS incident?
cards.a: A 3&1 or greater hazardous materials response (plus the utility company).
cards.why: M.P. 205.20A: "Request utility company to respond. Request a 3&1 or greater hazardous materials response."
opts: A 3&1 or greater hazardous materials response
A 2&1 structure fire assignment
A single engine and the utility company
A technical rescue team response

cards.q: A lithium-ion BESS is burning. Per M.P. 205.20A, what is the preferred tactic?
cards.a: Defensive firefighting: allow the battery to burn out while applying water to adjacent enclosures and exposures.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20A: "Response crews should allow the battery to burn out. Water should be applied to adjacent battery enclosures and exposures." Lithium-ion is not water reactive.
opts: Defensive: let it burn out and cool adjacent units and exposures
Offensive: flood the burning unit with foam
Smother it with dry chemical from 20 feet
Open the enclosure and cool the cells directly

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.20A, what color smoke from a BESS is a good indication of hazardous off-gassing?
cards.a: White colored smoke.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20A: "White colored smoke is a good indication of hazardous off-gassing."
opts: White
Black
Yellow-brown
Blue-gray

cards.q: You operate the disconnect on a residential BESS. Per M.P. 205.20A, is the battery now safe?
cards.a: No. The batteries still pose an electrical hazard from stranded energy.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20A: "Shutting off the disconnect does not remove the energy from the battery"; the batteries "still pose an electrical hazard due to the stranded energy."
opts: No, it still holds stranded energy
Yes, the disconnect drains the battery
Yes, once the inverter display goes dark
Only if the PV panels are also covered

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.20A, how often should temperature readings be taken on a residential battery during the monitoring period?
cards.a: At regular 10-minute intervals to identify trends.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20A: Readings "should be taken as early as possible and repeated at regular intervals (10 minutes) to identify trends." A 12-hour monitoring/cooling period is considered.
opts: Every 10 minutes
Every 30 minutes
Every hour
Every 5 minutes

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.20A, how far should you isolate the area around a residential BESS at minimum?
cards.a: A minimum of 40 feet; hazmat crews set the hot zone.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20A: "Isolate the area surrounding the residential BESS a minimum of 40 feet. Hazardous Materials crews will set a hot zone."
opts: 40 feet
150 feet
20 feet
100 feet

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.20B, what is the expected maximum voltage from a residential PV system?
cards.a: Up to 600 volts DC.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20B: Residential up to 600 V DC, commercial up to 1000 V DC, utility up to 1500 V DC.
opts: Up to 600 volts DC
Up to 1,000 volts DC
Up to 1,500 volts DC
Up to 240 volts AC

cards.q: A residential PV array is on fire and disconnects are operated. Per M.P. 205.20B, how do you apply water?
cards.a: A fog pattern of at least 10 degrees from at least 20 feet away.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20B: "A fog pattern delivered at a minimum of a 10-degree pattern from a minimum distance of 20 feet" is safe on PV installations up to 1000 volts.
opts: Fog at least a 10-degree pattern from at least 20 feet
Straight stream from at least 40 feet
Fog at least a 30-degree pattern from 10 feet
Solid stream from an aerial only

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.20B, what must you do before water is applied to a PV carport over a car fire?
cards.a: Operate the electrical disconnects that feed the system — it's mandatory.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20B: "It is mandatory to operate the disconnects prior to the application of water" on parking-lot PV installations.
opts: Operate the electrical disconnects that feed the system
Cover the panels with opaque tarps
Get approval from the utility representative
Confirm the voltage is under 600 volts

cards.q: The roof is covered with building-integrated PV shingles. Per M.P. 205.20B, can you conduct roof operations?
cards.a: No. Roof operations shall not be conducted on a building integrated PV tile or shingle roof.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20B: BIPV tiles are an electrical hazard and "extremely slippery." "Roof operations shall not be conducted" on them.
opts: No, roof operations shall not be done on BIPV roofs
Yes, after the rapid shutdown switch is operated
Yes, if crews stay on the ridge line
Only with a roof ladder and fall protection

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.20B, what must happen once a PV installation is identified on the fireground?
cards.a: Announce it on the tactical radio channel and have it acknowledged by Command.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20B: "The presence of a PV installation shall be announced on the tactical radio channel and acknowledged by Command."
opts: Announce it on the tactical channel; Command acknowledges
Notify Dispatch by phone only
Tell the first-in company officer face-to-face
Mark it on the tactical worksheet only

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.20B, what does operating the rapid shutdown switch do?
cards.a: It isolates the DC power for the PV system and confines the power to the array.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20B: Operate the rapid shut down switch "to isolate the DC power for the PV system and confine the power to the array." Older systems may lack it.
opts: Isolates DC power and confines it to the array
Drains all energy from the panels
Disconnects the house from the utility grid
Shuts off the battery storage system

cards.q: At a large PV utility generating station fire, per M.P. 205.20B, what do crews do?
cards.a: Remain outside the fence line, isolate the area, and protect exposures as needed.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20B: "We will not engage in any activities related to fire suppression inside the facility... All fire department personnel will remain outside the fence line."
opts: Stay outside the fence, isolate, and protect exposures
Attack from 20 feet with a 10-degree fog
Enter once the utility opens the main breaker
Apply foam to the inverters from an aerial

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.20B, what hose line size is required at a residential BESS?
cards.a: A charged 1 3/4" or larger line.
cards.why: M.P. 205.20B: "A charged hose line will be in place (1 3/4" or larger shall be used)."
opts: 1 3/4" or larger, charged
1 1/2" or larger, charged
2 1/2" only
A booster line is acceptable

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.22, when is the Surgical Emergency Response Team (SERT) used?
cards.a: When a patient needs a life- or limb-saving procedure beyond EMS capability or can't be extricated and transported in a reasonable time.
cards.why: M.P. 205.22: SERT is for procedures such as amputation due to inability to extricate. "Life before limb" is a life-saving measure, "not as a time saving measure."
opts: A patient needs life/limb-saving procedures and can't be extricated in time
Any multi-patient incident with more than 10 patients
Whenever a trauma patient's transport exceeds 30 minutes
Any amputation, to save scene time

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.22, how soon should SERT be assembled and ready to respond after a request?
cards.a: Within thirty (30) minutes.
cards.why: M.P. 205.22: "SERT should be assembled and ready to respond within thirty (30) minutes of a request."
opts: Within 30 minutes
Within 15 minutes
Within 60 minutes
Within 45 minutes

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.22, who transports the SERT from the trauma center to the scene?
cards.a: The closest available Battalion Chief, who also escorts them and gives a safety brief.
cards.why: M.P. 205.22: "The TRO will then send the closest available Battalion Chief to the trauma center closest to the incident to pick up the team."
opts: The closest available Battalion Chief
The closest ALS rescue
A police escort vehicle
The trauma center's own transport

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.22, how many SERT personnel can a Battalion Chief vehicle carry?
cards.a: Two SERT personnel.
cards.why: M.P. 205.22: "Battalion Chief Vehicles can only provide transportation for two SERT personnel."
opts: Two
Three
Four
One

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.22, what extra resource is added to every incident where SERT is requested?
cards.a: A second Command Officer (the next closest).
cards.why: M.P. 205.22: "A second Command Officer will be added to all incidents where the SERT is requested."
opts: A second Command Officer
A second ALS rescue
A heavy rescue company
A hazmat team

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.22, who documents patient care at the scene of a SERT incident?
cards.a: The charting paramedic.
cards.why: M.P. 205.22: "The charting paramedic will be responsible for documentation related to patient care at the scene," including surgical care in the field.
opts: The charting paramedic
The SERT trauma surgeon only
The Battalion Chief escort
The treatment sector officer

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.23, how is a Medical Response (MR) unit staffed?
cards.a: A 4-person crew: two firefighters, one engineer and one captain.
cards.why: M.P. 205.23: MR staffing is a "4-person crew including two firefighters, one engineer and one captain."
opts: 4: two firefighters, an engineer, and a captain
2 trained firefighters of any rank
3: a captain, an engineer, and a paramedic
4 paramedics with no company officer

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.23, can an MR replace an engine company at a structure fire?
cards.a: No. MRs supplement firefighting duties but cannot replace an engine, ladder or squad.
cards.why: M.P. 205.23: "MRs cannot replace an engine, ladder, or squad company for fire suppression, rescue, and special operations type incidents." They carry no hose, water or ladders.
opts: No, it can only supplement firefighting as assigned
Yes, if it is staffed ALS
Yes, when no engine is within 4 minutes
Only for the first-due assignment

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.23, an MR may respond without another unit's support only on which nature code categories?
cards.a: BLS, ALS, SERV and MISC SERVICE.
cards.why: M.P. 205.23: "MR Units may only respond to incidents without the support of another unit on the following nature code categories: BLS, ALS, SERV and MISC SERVICE."
opts: BLS, ALS, SERV and MISC SERVICE
BLS and low acuity codes only
ALS, structure fires, and SERV
Any code if staffed with four

cards.q: An LA unit is closest to a cardiac arrest across a city line. Per M.P. 205.23, what happens?
cards.a: It is deployed across the boundary to supplement the response, not in replacement of other units.
cards.why: M.P. 205.23: LA units are deployed across municipal boundaries on imminent-threat calls when closest; "they shall not be deployed in replacement of other units."
opts: It responds to supplement, not replace, other units
It is not sent, since LA units are BLS-only
It replaces the engine as the assigned unit
It responds only if the other city approves

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.23, how should an LA unit be used at a working fire?
cards.a: Only assigned by command to support an appropriately staffed, NFPA 1710 compliant, 4-person company.
cards.why: M.P. 205.23: LA units "should only be assigned by command to support an appropriately staffed, NFPA 1710 compliant, 4-person fire company," like a 2-person rescue.
opts: Only to support a 4-person NFPA 1710 compliant company
As the first-due fire attack company
As the RIC team on any fire
Never; LA units cannot be at fires

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.24, who has final authority to accept or decline a UAS mission?
cards.a: The Pilot in Command; no one, regardless of rank, may order a pilot to accept a mission.
cards.why: M.P. 205.24: "The pilot is ultimately responsible for the UAS operation, and their authority is absolute." No member "regardless of rank" may order a pilot to accept a mission.
opts: The pilot in command (PIC)
The Incident Commander
The UAS Program Manager
The on-duty Shift Commander

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.24, what is the maximum altitude for PFD drone operations without a waiver?
cards.a: 400 feet AGL, or if higher, within 400 feet of a structure.
cards.why: M.P. 205.24: "Operations may occur up to a maximum altitude of 400 feet AGL or, if higher than 400 AGL, remain within 400 feet of a structure."
opts: 400 ft AGL, or within 400 ft of a structure if higher
200 ft AGL anywhere in the city
500 ft AGL, or 100 ft above any structure
400 ft above mean sea level

cards.q: You're flying a drone at a brush fire when a DPS helicopter arrives with no deconfliction training. Per M.P. 205.24, what do you do?
cards.a: Ground the UAS; manned aircraft have priority.
cards.why: M.P. 205.24: "All UAS flights shall be grounded upon arrival of approved government manned aircraft... unless coordinated flight training has occurred with that agency."
opts: Ground the drone
Drop below 200 feet and continue
Move to the opposite flank and continue
Continue but stay within line of sight

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.24, when is a Visual Observer required?
cards.a: A Visual Observer is required for night flights.
cards.why: M.P. 205.24: "A visual observer is required for night flights"; teams otherwise use a pilot and VO when possible.
opts: For all night flights
Only beyond visual line of sight
Only within 5 miles of an airport
Only for flights over 200 feet

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.24, how soon after drinking alcohol may a member act as a PIC or VO?
cards.a: Not within eight (8) hours after consuming any alcoholic beverage.
cards.why: M.P. 205.24: "No member shall act as a PIC or a VO within eight hours (8) after consumption of any alcoholic beverage."
opts: Not within 8 hours
Not within 12 hours
Not within 24 hours
Not within 4 hours

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.24, what is the maximum time a pilot may act as PIC?
cards.a: No more than 10 consecutive hours in any 24-hour period.
cards.why: M.P. 205.24: "No pilot may act as a PIC for more than 10 consecutive hours in any 24-hour period."
opts: 10 consecutive hours in any 24-hour period
8 consecutive hours in any 24-hour period
12 consecutive hours per shift
14 hours in any 24-hour period

cards.q: Your VO loses sight of the drone. Per M.P. 205.24, what does the RPIC do first?
cards.a: Place the aircraft into hover mode while the RPIC and VO try to reestablish visual contact.
cards.why: M.P. 205.24: The RPIC places it in hover; if not reacquired within a reasonable time, the RPIC initiates the Return to Home sequence.
opts: Put the drone in hover while both try to regain sight
Immediately start Return to Home
Land the drone at its current position
Climb to 400 feet to get it in view

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.24, to stay current, how many takeoffs and landings must a PFD pilot log, and over what period?
cards.a: At least three takeoffs and landings in the preceding 90 days in each type of aircraft.
cards.why: M.P. 205.24: Pilots "must record at least three (3) takeoffs and landings in the preceding 90-days in each type aircraft."
opts: 3 in the preceding 90 days
3 in the preceding 30 days
5 in the preceding 90 days
10 in the preceding 180 days

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.24, which use of the PFD drone is prohibited?
cards.a: Use of facial recognition technology of any kind is prohibited.
cards.why: M.P. 205.24: UAS information may not be collected or used to "utilize facial recognition surveillance technologies or software of any kind."
opts: Facial recognition of people in a crowd
Mapping hot spots at a brush fire
Locating a lost hiker on a preserve
Checking a fire roof for structural collapse
